test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 23 Sept, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: For two circles of radius 7 units and (7)/(2) units, whose centres are 15 units apart, what is the length of the direct common tangent in units? (Correct to 3 decimal places.)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct Common Tangent = √[d² − (r₁ − r₂)²]

DCT = √[15² − (7 − 3.5)²]

DCT = √[225 − 12.25]

DCT = √212.75 ≈ 14.586 units

**∴ The correct answer is 14.586 units.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of first circle, r₁ = 7 units

Radius of second circle, r₂ = 3.5 units

Distance between their centres, d = 15 units

 
 
 
• 
 d = 15
 
 C₁
 
 C₂
 
• 
 r₁=7
 
• 
 r₂=3.5
 
• 
 DCT = ?

**Formula Used:**

Direct Common Tangent (DCT) = √[d² − (r₁ − r₂)²]

**Calculations:**

⇒ DCT = √[15² − (7 − 3.5)²]

⇒ DCT = √[225 − (3.5)²]

⇒ DCT = √[225 − 12.25]

⇒ DCT = √212.75

⇒ DCT ≈ 14.586 units

**∴ The correct answer is 14.586 units.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Transverse Common Tangent (TCT)

A common tangent that intersects the line segment joining the centres of the two circles. Its length is calculated as TCT = √[d² − (r₁ + r₂)²].

Number of Common Tangents

When the distance (d) between centres is greater than the sum of radii (r₁ + r₂), the circles do not touch, and exactly 4 common tangents can be drawn (2 direct and 2 transverse).

Touching Circles

If two circles touch each other externally (d = r₁ + r₂), they have exactly 3 common tangents. If they touch internally (d = |r₁ − r₂|), they have only 1 common tangent.
